clue.text: Record of things wanted is brought in whilst out

indicators.note: something brought in is placed inside, so one piece goes within the other
out suggests disorder or being put out of place, so these letters get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopping list gets brought indoors while its owner is away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' reads as 'away from home', but it signals the shuffle; 'brought in' then places the short word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A wish list is an itemised note of the presents or purchases a person hopes to get.

clue.text: Capital used to be chilly and damp, upon reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the combined letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: past tense of 'to be'
raw weather is cold and wet

explanation.surface: Someone recalls that a city used to have cold, wet weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upon reflection' reads like 'thinking it over', but it turns the whole string back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Warsaw is the seat of government of Poland, its largest city.

clue.text: Show places etc abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered or astray, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A travel note: shows are put on in various places overseas and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is a visually striking public performance or display, in the same way that a show is.

clue.text: Fast runner, potentially, always allowed to go round

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: let means permitted
ever means at all times

explanation.surface: A sprinter has always been permitted to run laps.
explanation.walkthrough: A leveret is a young hare, which will potentially grow into a fast runner, hence the qualifier.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveret is a hare in its first year, so a creature that is a quick runner in the making.

clue.text: Drink in country with cast

blocks.note: an island nation in South-East Asia
to sling is to throw or cast

explanation.surface: Someone has a drink abroad while wearing a plaster cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a noun (a plaster cast) but is the verb meaning throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A Singapore sling is a gin-based cocktail first mixed at Raffles Hotel.

clue.text: Keep limited opener for Somerset at crease

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its very beginning, so just its first letter is taken

blocks.note: first letter of the county name
to crimp is to press into small folds or creases

explanation.surface: A cricket report: Somerset's opening batsman keeps the score low while at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: The crease is where a batter stands in cricket, and Somerset is an English county side, but here 'crease' just means a fold.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to economise, keeping spending or supplies tightly restricted.

clue.text: Remarkably typical college girl in charge

blocks.note: C is an abbreviation for college
a lass is a girl
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A female student is put in charge, which is quite characteristic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remarkably' looks like an anagram signal but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic example is one so representative of its kind that it is a textbook case.

clue.text: Expression used by one daughter on the Isle of Man

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
the standard abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A girl on the Isle of Man uses a local turn of phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a self-governing island in the Irish Sea; 'on' simply places the IOM after the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a fixed phrase whose meaning is not deducible from its words, a kind of verbal expression.

clue.text: Girl embarrassed producing old postage stamp

blocks.note: a girl's name
red-faced with embarrassment

explanation.surface: A blushing girl produces a rare stamp from her collection.
explanation.definitionFit: The Penny Red was the British one-penny stamp issued from 1841 to 1879, successor to the Penny Black.

clue.text: Enjoy article on Victorian novelist a lot

blocks.note: to like is to enjoy
the definite article
Charles Dickens, the Victorian author

explanation.surface: A reader is urged to enjoy an essay about Dickens very much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The dickens' is an old euphemism for the devil, so 'like the dickens' means intensely or hugely.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'like the dickens' is an intensifier meaning very much or extremely, as in 'it hurt like the dickens'.

clue.text: English resort, one on the Isle of Wight duke disregarded

indicators.note: what is disregarded is ignored and left out, so the duke's letter is dropped

blocks.clueFragment: one on the Isle of Wight
blocks.note: Ryde is a town on the Isle of Wight
D is an abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A seaside town is compared with one on the Isle of Wight, its aristocrat ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Wight is an island off England's south coast; removing D from RYDE leaves RYE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a historic town in East Sussex, a Cinque Port that is now a tourist destination.

clue.text: See sign of support

blocks.note: v. is the abbreviation for vide, Latin for see
an indication is a sign

explanation.surface: An instruction to look for a sign of backing.
explanation.walkthrough: V for 'see' comes from the Latin vide, used in reference books.
explanation.definitionFit: Vindication is justification or confirmation that a claim was right, a form of backing for it.

clue.text: Substitute to change number at end of game

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: to alter is to change
N is an abbreviation for number
taken as written
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A manager makes a substitution late in a match to change a player's number.
explanation.definitionFit: An alternate is a stand-in or reserve, chiefly in American usage, who takes another's place.

clue.text: Boringly repetitive, for example, crossing Maine

indicators.note: crossing here means spanning across, so the outer word straddles the inner one

blocks.note: say, as in 'say, apples', means for example
ME is the postal abbreviation of the US state

explanation.surface: Someone finds a long drive across Maine monotonous.
explanation.walkthrough: Samey is informal British English, little used in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Samey is an informal British adjective for things so alike as to be dull and monotonous.

clue.text: Teach those troubled by wound to focus on what's important

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed or agitated, so the letters are stirred into another order

blocks.note: a cut is a wound
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to tutor pupils upset by an injury so they concentrate on essentials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' could be read as the past of wind, but it is the injury.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut to the chase is an idiom for skipping preliminaries and getting to the main point.

clue.text: Pleasant, a US actor ringing about European

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the actor's name surrounds the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
Clark Gable, Hollywood star of Gone with the Wind
re means concerning or about
E is an abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A charming American film star is encircling a European.
explanation.walkthrough: The actor's name is split after its first letter to take the inserted pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreeable describes something or someone nice and enjoyable, a close synonym of pleasant.

clue.text: Atelier husband found in Notts town

indicators.note: something found in a place sits inside it, so one letter goes within the town's name

blocks.note: Worksop is a town in Nottinghamshire
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband turns up at a studio in a Nottinghamshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Notts is the short form of Nottinghamshire, an English county in the Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or craftsman's studio, which is a kind of workshop.

clue.text: Welsh hero surprisingly wore down foe, ultimately capturing valley

indicators.note: something that happens surprisingly comes out unexpectedly, so the letters emerge in an unexpected order
ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter of the word is used
capturing means holding inside, so the rearranged letters enclose another word

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
last letter of the word
a glen is a narrow valley

explanation.surface: A Welsh champion unexpectedly exhausted an enemy and in the end seized a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of WORE DOWN plus E is split around GLEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Owain Glyndwr, anglicised as Owen Glendower, led the Welsh revolt against English rule in the early 1400s.

clue.text: Book an old pop group

blocks.note: first meaning: the first book of the Bible
second meaning: the English rock band of Phil Collins and Peter Gabriel

explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' reads like a verb (to reserve a band), but it names a book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is shared by the opening book of the Old Testament and a British band formed in 1967.

clue.text: Bandy words in castle

indicators.note: to bandy is to toss back and forth, so the letters get knocked about into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: People exchange heated words inside a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Windsor Castle in Berkshire is a royal residence of the British monarch.

clue.text: Express agreement when told to go

blocks.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
someone sent away has been told to go

explanation.surface: Someone nods along when ordered to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To assent is to agree or give consent, the verb counterpart of saying yes.

clue.text: Boy another left out

indicators.note: out means removed or excluded, so the letter for left is taken away

blocks.note: another boy's name
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: One lad is excluded from a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' stands for a second boy's name, which is not stated; dropping L from KELVIN gives KEVIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Kevin is a common male first name, so it stands for a boy.

clue.text: Very sick adult in holiday home

blocks.note: V is an abbreviation for very
ill means sick
A is the film certificate for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up falls badly ill while staying in rented holiday accommodation.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a detached house often rented by tourists in warm resorts.

clue.text: More than one publican doesn't tell the truth about ugly scene

indicators.note: something ugly is misshapen, so the following letters are twisted into another order
about means around, so the first word wraps around the other letters

blocks.note: lies means says what is false
letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Several pub landlords lie about a nasty fight on their premises.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a publican, who runs a pub, must hold a licence to sell alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A licensee is the holder of a licence, in Britain chiefly the landlord of a pub; plural matches 'more than one'.

clue.text: Small backers chasing underworld gang

blocks.note: hell is the underworld
S is an abbreviation for small
angels are financial backers, especially of shows

explanation.surface: Little investors are pursuing a criminal gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chasing' means coming after, so the backers and their size come after the underworld; angels is theatre slang for investors.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hells Angels are a worldwide motorcycle club often described as an outlaw gang.

clue.text: Reportedly purchase extra

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say, so the word is judged by its spoken sound

blocks.note: to buy is to purchase

explanation.surface: A rumour that someone bought something additional.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is a run scored when the ball passes the batter untouched; it counts among the extras.
explanation.definitionFit: A bye is one of the extras in cricket, runs not credited to a batter.

clue.text: Quiet lift gets approval

blocks.note: p for piano, the musical direction for soft
to raise is to lift

explanation.surface: A discreet boost earns someone a word of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' and 'quiet' suggest a silent elevator, but they are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Praise is commendation, the expression of approval of someone.

clue.text: Hungry? Tureen is specially prepared

indicators.note: something specially prepared has been made up anew, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner is peckish because a soup tureen has been made ready.
explanation.definitionFit: Esurient is a literary word for greedy or ravenous, from the Latin for being hungry.
